article.body_html:
If your shift ends at midnight, a monthly bike has to work at 00:30, when almost nothing else is open. Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà is open 09:00–21:00 daily, so plan as if a problem between 21:00 and 09:00 is yours to handle until the shop opens, and ask at booking whether anyone can be reached at night. That changes what matters in a monthly rental: the lights, how tired you are at the end of the shift, where the bike sleeps, and what you do when something goes wrong in the middle of the night.

What a month costs per shift

The reference price of a manual bike for one month is 1,000,000 to 1,200,000 VND, and of an automatic bike 1,200,000 to 2,000,000 VND. Both are reference prices; ask the shop to confirm the bike and the rate when you book. Spread over 22 shifts a month, the arithmetic is simple:

BikeMonthPer shift (22 shifts)
Manual1,000,000 to 1,200,000 VNDabout 45,500 to 54,500 VND
Automatic1,200,000 to 2,000,000 VNDabout 54,500 to 90,900 VND

That is the rental alone. Fuel and parking come on top, and parking is the one to settle first, so it gets its own section below. Count your own shifts: with 26 instead of 22, the manual range falls to about 38,500 to 46,200 VND per shift.

Lights: test them at the hour you will use them

In daylight a headlight proves nothing. Before you accept the bike, ask to switch on the low beam, the high beam, the indicators and the brake light, and have someone stand behind the bike while you squeeze each brake lever. On the first night, ride a short, familiar, well-lit road at low speed to see how far the beam reaches. Then repeat the check once a week, because a bulb that fails at 00:30 is a safety problem, not an inconvenience.

If the brake light or the headlight stops working on the way home, stop in a lit place and do not carry on riding in the dark on the strength of "it is only a few streets". Call the shop when it opens and tell it exactly which light failed and when. Light-coloured or reflective clothing helps other riders see you, though it does not replace working lights.

Fatigue at the end of a shift

Riding after a long shift is different from riding after a rest. Reaction time and attention suffer when you are tired, and the signs, such as heavy eyelids, drifting within the lane or missing a turn you know well, are the same ones that appear on a long day trip. The guide to fatigue, rest stops and a return cutoff lists them. For a night worker the practical answer is a plan for the nights when you should not ride: a way home that does not use the bike, and a safe place to leave it until the next day. If you have been drinking, the bike stays where it is.

Where the bike sleeps

  • Choose a lit, busy spot. A well-lit place where people pass is better than a dark corner, even if it is a few steps further from your door.
  • Lock every time. Use the steering lock and any lock that came with the bike, and ask the shop what locks and security a monthly rental includes instead of assuming; Rental Bike Locking in Hanoi: A Practical Parking Routine gives a routine for the nightly lock-up.
  • Keep valuables out of the storage space. Take the helmet, papers and anything of value with you.
  • Photograph the parked bike. A time-stamped photo of the bike and its surroundings is useful if a problem appears later.
  • Ask about parking before you move in. If the building or workplace has parking rules or a fee, learn them before the first night; changing hotels during a monthly rental shows how to keep the parking location on record.

When something goes wrong at 00:30

The shop is closed, so settle the plan in advance. Stop safely, photograph the bike and the place, lock it or push it somewhere safer, and get home another way. Then call the shop on 0334 699 969 when it opens at 09:00 and give it the time, the place and the symptom. If the bike will not start, the information to send the shop tells you what to note before you call. Do not arrange a repair on your own before you have spoken to the shop. Hanoi Motorbike Breakdown After 21:00: Prepare a Safe Waiting Plan covers the waiting itself in more detail.

The shop's monthly rental page describes the longer rental, and renters who stay a month or more will find related guides in the Weekly & Monthly Rentals category.
